svg.title: A public hospital network: the fourteen layers
svg.desc: A building with fourteen floors, one per layer, naming the main systems of a public hospital network. The ground floor is infrastructure and compute (R01): state data centres, private cloud, Australian cloud regions and vendor-hosted EMR. The data platform (R02) holds the clinical data repository, the data warehouse, state collections and registries. The integration fabric (R03) holds the integration engine, the FHIR server, secure messaging and the My Health Record gateway. Systems of record (R04) hold the EMR, the PAS, the laboratory system (LIS), and radiology (RIS and PACS). They also hold pharmacy, the patient index, incidents, and HR and rostering. Line of business (R05) holds emergency, theatres, maternity, ICU, oncology, bed flow and medical devices. Intelligence and learning (R06) holds EMR alerts, early warning scores, radiology AI, speech recognition and ambient scribes. The agent platform (R07) is mostly absent today: RPA bots, chatbots, virtual triage and vendor agents. Productivity (R08) holds Microsoft 365, Teams for MDTs, fax servers and the policy library. Experience and channels (R09) holds SMS and letters, the booking centre, telehealth, the patient portal and GP portals. Security and identity (R10) holds Entra ID, tap-badge sign-on, NASH certificates and security monitoring. Governance (R11) holds clinical governance, NSQHS accreditation, the privacy officer and the AI governance group. Observability (R12) holds application monitoring, integration error queues and IT service management. The operating model (R13) holds the digital health division, the referral hub and the quality and safety unit. The top floor, agent data engineering (R14), holds document capture, patient index stewardship and terminology mapping. Bold boxes mark the main systems the four use cases lean on most.
